tapeLine: Thursday 5 November: S&P 500 −4.36% to 7,353.73, its worst day since April 2025; Dow −1,833.06 (−3.44%) to 51,523.06; Nasdaq Composite −5.52% to 24,315.00, in correction territory, per reports dated 5 Nov. Friday futures were not found.
matters:
Chip and AI stocks led a broad sell-off on Thursday, reversing Wednesday’s post-midterm rally, when the Dow gained more than 1,500 points on a Democratic win. Nvidia, Micron and AMD were among the hardest hit, and all eleven S&P sectors closed lower, per reports dated 5 Nov.

Reports tied the drop to fears that a Democratic sweep could bring AI regulation and slow data-center construction. Outlets differ on the cause; that is the reported explanation, not a confirmed one.

macro: Politics — Democrats won control of both chambers in Tuesday’s midterms; stocks rallied Wednesday, then fell Thursday on AI-regulation concerns, per reports dated 4–5 Nov.
Earnings — AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.377 billion after the close on 3 Nov, per reports dated 4 Nov; the stock was among Thursday’s decliners.

regime.tag: The Wednesday post-election rally was erased on Thursday: a chip-led sell-off took the Nasdaq into correction.
regime.sizing: Whether Thursday’s drop extends or steadies is unresolved; no Friday data was found.

secondOrder: Two sharp moves in opposite directions in two sessions on the same election news. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: The prior brief left open whether the chip rebound would hold after AMD’s results, and carried reports that AI-sweep worries had eased. It did not hold: chips led a sell-off on Thursday and the S&P 500 fell 4.36%.
The prior brief’s caution that reports differed on breadth and that the Tuesday gain was narrow was borne out by the sharp reversal that followed.
Yield behaviour still cannot be graded: no dated, sourced yield levels were found.
